post.description: Creates an inbox that sends and receives email at an address on one of your domains. The domain must belong to the team. Without `forwarding`, the domain must have receiving enabled, with DKIM and SPF verified and the inbound MX record verified or pending. With `forwarding` set to `true`, the domain only needs DKIM and SPF verified for sending, and Resend generates a `receiving_address` on the team inbound domain, and a team without an inbound domain gets a 422. A domain that does not meet these rules returns a 422 validation_error. An address or receiving address that is already in use returns a 409. A team that has reached the inbox limit of its plan returns a 403 validation_error. A blocked account returns a 451.

get.description: Returns the inboxes of the team, newest first. The list items carry fewer fields than a single inbox. Retrieve an inbox to get all its fields. The `after` and `before` cursors take an inbox ID, and only one of them can be passed, or the request returns a 422. A value that is not a UUID returns a 422, and an unknown ID returns a 404.

get.summary: Retrieve a list of inbox threads
get.description: Returns the threads in an inbox, most recently active first. A thread is a conversation made up of one or more emails. The `after` and `before` cursors take a thread ID, and only one of them can be passed. A cursor that is not a UUID, such as a date, returns a 422 validation_error. A cursor thread that is not in the selected folders returns a 404. To find threads by text, sender, recipient, attachment, or date, use the search threads endpoint.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Comma-separated folders to list, for example `inbox,sent`. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error. A thread is returned when any of its emails is in one of the folders, so a thread in `inbox` with an email you sent matches both `inbox` and `sent`. Defaults to `inbox`, or to `inbox,archive,sent` when `labels` is set. `spam` and `trash` are only included when you name them.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Comma-separated label IDs. Returns threads with any of these labels. Up to 50 IDs. An ID that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: `true` returns threads where every email is read. `false` returns threads with at least one unread email. Only the literal values `true` and `false` are accepted.

get.summary: Search the threads of an inbox
get.description: Finds threads by the text of their emails, who sent or received them, whether they have attachments, and their dates. Results are ordered by latest activity, newest first, and paginate like the list threads endpoint, so a cursor that is not a thread ID returns a 422. Search can be up to about a minute behind new emails. Different parameters combine, so a thread must match all of them. `folders`, `labels`, and `read` apply to the thread. `query`, `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `has_attachment`, `start_date`, and `end_date` must all match the same email in the thread. When any of these email filters is set, the matching email must itself be in one of `folders`. For `sent`, that means an email the inbox sent. When more than 10,000 threads match, search covers the 10,000 with the newest matching email.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free text to search for in the subject, body, sender, recipients, and attachment names. Every word must match. Wrap words in double quotes to match an exact phrase. Start a word or quoted phrase with `-` to exclude it. Max 256 characters and 32 words.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Comma-separated senders. Each value matches part of the sender's address or name, without case. Returns threads that match any of them. Up to 20 values. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Comma-separated recipients, matched the same way as `from`. Up to 20 values. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error.

parameters.name: cc
parameters.description: Comma-separated CC recipients, matched the same way as `from`. Up to 20 values. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error.

parameters.name: bcc
parameters.description: Comma-separated BCC recipients, matched the same way as `from`. Up to 20 values. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error.

parameters.name: has_attachment
parameters.description: `true` matches emails with an attachment. `false` matches emails without one. Only the literal values `true` and `false` are accepted.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Matches emails sent on or after this date. Accepts a date like `2026-09-01` or an ISO 8601 timestamp, in UTC unless the timestamp has an offset. An empty value returns a 422.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Matches emails sent on or before this date. Same formats as `start_date`. A date covers that whole day, so `start_date=2026-09-01&end_date=2026-09-30` covers all of September. A timestamp is used as given. An `end_date` before `start_date` returns a 422 validation_error. An empty value returns a 422.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Comma-separated folders to search, for example `inbox,sent`. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error. A thread is returned when any of its emails is in one of the folders. Defaults to `inbox`, or to `inbox,archive,sent` when `labels` is set. `spam` and `trash` are only included when you name them.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Comma-separated label IDs. Returns threads with any of these labels. Up to 50 IDs. An ID that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404. Repeating the parameter returns a 422 validation_error.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: `true` returns threads where every email is read. `false` returns threads with at least one unread email. Only the literal values `true` and `false` are accepted.

get.description: Returns the thread summary. The emails in the thread are listed with the list thread emails endpoint.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

patch.description: Marks a thread read or unread, or moves it to a folder. At least one of `read` or `folder` is required. To change the labels of a thread, use the add, set, and remove thread labels endpoints. This endpoint ignores the removed `add_label_ids` and `remove_label_ids` fields, so a body with only those fields returns a 422 validation_error. Moving a thread out of `trash` restores it and clears its deletion deadline. The changes apply in this order: `read`, then `folder`. They are not atomic.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

delete.description: Moves the thread to `trash` and schedules it for deletion in 30 days. This is reversible. To restore the thread, update its `folder` to `inbox`, `archive`, or `spam`, which also clears the deletion deadline.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

post.summary: Add labels to an inbox thread
post.description: Applies one or more labels to the thread. Labels already on the thread stay on it. The response lists every label on the thread after the change. A label ID that is not a label of the inbox returns a 404 `Label not found.`, and nothing changes. A thread that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404 `Thread not found.`. To replace the labels of the thread, use the set thread labels endpoint.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

put.summary: Set the labels of an inbox thread
put.description: Replaces every label on the thread with the given labels, in one atomic change. Labels on the thread that are not in the list are taken off it. The labels themselves are kept. An empty array takes every label off the thread. The response lists every label on the thread after the change. A label ID that is not a label of the inbox returns a 404 `Label not found.`, and nothing changes. A thread that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404 `Thread not found.`.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

delete.summary: Remove a label from an inbox thread
delete.description: Takes one label off the thread. The label itself is kept, and stays on every other thread that carries it. To delete the label, use the remove inbox label endpoint. The response lists every label on the thread after the change. A label that is not on the thread returns a 200 with the current labels. A label ID that is not a label of the inbox returns a 404 `Label not found.`. A thread that does not exist in the inbox returns a 404 `Thread not found.`.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

get.summary: Retrieve a list of thread emails
get.description: Returns the messages of a thread, oldest first. Pass the `id` of the last message as `after` to get the next, newer page. Pass the `id` of the first message as `before` to get the previous, older page. Passing both `after` and `before`, or a cursor that is not a UUID, returns a 422. A cursor that is not a message of the thread returns a 404.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: emailId
parameters.description: The Email ID, as returned in `data[].id` by the list thread emails endpoint.

post.description: Sends a reply from the inbox address right away, with no stored draft. The `to` recipients come from the message you reply to. For a message the inbox received, the reply goes to its `Reply-To` addresses, or to its sender when it has no `Reply-To`. For a message the inbox sent, the reply goes to that message's `to` recipients. Set `reply_all` to also copy the other recipients of the message. The reply threads under the message through the `In-Reply-To` and `References` headers. When no recipient can be found for the reply, the request returns a 422. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key for the request, so the reply is sent only once. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first successful (2xx) response, with the `idempotent-replayed: true` header. A failed request is not stored, so it can be retried with the same key. Reusing the key with a different body, or while the first request is still running, returns a 409. An empty key, or one longer than 256 characters, returns a 400 `invalid_idempotency_key`. [Learn more](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/idempotency-keys)

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: emailId
parameters.description: The Email ID of the message to reply to, as returned in `data[].id` by the list thread emails endpoint.

post.description: Forwards a message from the inbox address right away, with no stored draft. The original message is quoted under a forwarded-message banner, below the optional `html` or `text` note. The attachments of the original message are sent with the forward, together with any `attachments` you add. The request returns a 422 when they exceed 25 MB of `content` in total. An original attachment that was sent from a URL (`path`) cannot be forwarded, and the request returns a 422. The whole email, encoded, can be at most 40 MB, or the request returns a 422.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key for the request, so the forward is sent only once. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first successful (2xx) response, with the `idempotent-replayed: true` header. A failed request is not stored, so it can be retried with the same key. Reusing the key with a different body, or while the first request is still running, returns a 409. An empty key, or one longer than 256 characters, returns a 400 `invalid_idempotency_key`. [Learn more](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/idempotency-keys)

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: emailId
parameters.description: The Email ID of the message to forward, as returned in `data[].id` by the list thread emails endpoint.

get.description: Returns the unsent drafts on the inbox, most recently updated first. The `after` and `before` cursors take a Draft ID from the current page, and only one of them can be passed. A cursor that is not a UUID, or both cursors together, return a 422. A cursor that is not an unsent draft on this inbox returns a 404.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: The Inbox ID or the inbox email address, such as `support@acme.com`. A value that contains `@` must be a valid email address, and any other value must be a UUID, or the request returns a 422. The address match is case-insensitive and never falls back to the inbox `name`. An address that matches no inbox returns a 404.

post.description: Creates an unsent draft on the inbox. Omit `thread_id` and `reply_to_email_id` for a draft that starts a new thread. Pass both together for a reply draft in an existing thread. A reply draft without `to` is addressed to the sender of the email it replies to, or to its Reply-To when set. For an email the inbox sent, it defaults to that email's `to` recipients. Send `to: []` to leave it empty. At least one of `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `text`, `html` or `attachments` must be non-empty. The combined recipients of `to`, `cc` and `bcc` cannot exceed 50.
